- The purple ring p(39) is at ~(36, 46)
- The gray square G(42) is at ~(38, 47) (was G(44) before)
So clicking on O(11) moved the white diamond to ~(14, 27) and also moved the orange square O(8) from ~(14, 27) to ~(15, 19). The gray square G(5) also moved from ~(9, 49) to ~(12, 24).
Wait, this is confusing. Let me re-examine:
- Before clicking O(11): G(5) at ~(9, 49), G(7) at ~(12, 24), O(11) at ~(14, 27), G(25) at ~(21, 8), p(41) at ~(36, 46), G(44) at ~(38, 47)
- After clicking O(11): G(5) at ~(12, 24), O(8) at ~(15, 19), G(23) at ~(21, 8), p(39) at ~(36, 46), G(42) at ~(38, 47), W(7) at ~(14, 27)
So:
- G(5) moved from ~(9, 49) to ~(12, 24) (was G(7)'s position)
- G(7) disappeared (or merged with G(5))
- O(11) moved from ~(14, 27) to ~(15, 19) (now O(8))
- G(25) is now G(23) at ~(21, 8) (same position)
- p(41) is now p(39) at ~(36, 46) (same position)
- G(44) is now G(42) at ~(38, 47) (same position)
- W(7) appeared at ~(14, 27) (was O(11)'s position)
So clicking on O(11) moved the white diamond to ~(14, 27) and also moved the orange square O(11) to ~(15, 19). The gray square G(5) also moved from ~(9, 49) to ~(12, 24), which was G(7)'s position.
This is getting complicated. Let me think about what the game mechanics might be:
1. The white diamond is the player avatar.
2. Clicking on objects moves the white diamond to those positions.
3. When the white diamond moves to a position, it swaps with the object at that position.
4. The gray squares and orange square move to new positions when the white diamond swaps with them.
Actually, I think the game might be about "collecting" objects by swapping the white diamond with them. The white diamond swaps with the object at the clicked position, and the object moves to a new position.
Let me try clicking on the purple ring to see if the white diamond swaps with it.

# Click on the purple ring at ~(36, 46)
action([{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 36, 'col': 46}])

nodes = seg['nodes']

for n in nodes:
    if n['color'] not in ('B', 'W', 'g') and n['pixels'] >= 5:
        center = (sum(b[0] for b in n['boundary'])//len(n['boundary']),
                  sum(b[1] for b in n['boundary'])//len(n['boundary']))

# Check for white diamond

print(f"\nWhite objects: {len(w_nodes)}")
for wn in w_nodes:
    center = (sum(b[0] for b in wn['boundary'])//len(wn['boundary']),
              sum(b[1] for b in wn['boundary'])//len(wn['boundary']))
    print(f"  W({wn['id']}) px={wn['pixels']} ~{center}")
